details.description: QwQ-32B is a 32.5-billion-parameter reasoning model from Alibaba's Qwen team, built on the Qwen2.5 architecture and released in March 2025 under the Apache 2.0 license. Unlike Qwen's conventional instruction-tuned models, QwQ is trained with supervised fine-tuning and large-scale reinforcement learning so it can think through problems before answering, and Qwen reports it reaches performance comparable to DeepSeek-R1 (a 671-billion-parameter model with 37B activated) despite its much smaller size. It also integrates agent-related capabilities, letting it reason while calling tools and adapting to feedback from its environment.
advantages: Qwen reports QwQ-32B achieves performance comparable to DeepSeek-R1, a 671-billion-parameter model (37B activated), despite QwQ-32B having only 32.5B parameters, per the launch blog post.
Integrates agent-related capabilities, letting it reason while using tools and adapt its reasoning based on environmental feedback, per the launch blog post.
Released under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face and ModelScope, per the launch blog post.
131,072-token context window, using YaRN scaling for prompts beyond 8,192 tokens, per the model card.
disadvantages: Requires enabling YaRN to reliably handle prompts longer than 8,192 tokens; without it, the model card reports handling of long sequences is comparatively weak.
Text-only: the model card documents no vision or audio input.
Trained on the earlier Qwen2.5 architecture rather than Qwen's newer model generations, per the model card.
use_cases: Complex, multi-step reasoning tasks, especially math and coding problems
Agentic tasks that require tool use and adapting to environment feedback
Long-context analysis up to 131,072 tokens (with YaRN enabled)

sources.title: QwQ-32B: Embracing the Power of Reinforcement Learning | Qwen

notes: The launch blog's benchmark comparison (vs. DeepSeek-R1-Distilled-Qwen-32B, DeepSeek-R1-Distilled-Llama-70B, o1-mini, DeepSeek-R1) is presented only as a chart image, so no numeric scores could be read from the page text; left evaluations empty rather than guess. The Hugging Face page also carries an 'Eval Results' widget with figures such as MMLU-Pro 69.07 and LEXam scores, but these are community-submitted third-party results (sourced from a dataset named 'evaleval/EEE_datastore', not Qwen's own reported numbers or a named leaderboard like Artificial Analysis/LMArena/MTEB), so they were excluded per the instruction to use only the maker's own numbers or a named leaderboard. No deprecation or legacy notice was found on Qwen's model card or launch blog; the catalog's facts also carry no deprecation_date.
